task: Jess from sales asks what your project actually does. She isn't technical. Explain it in plain words and answer her questions.
zh: 销售部的 Jess 问你的项目到底是做什么的。她不懂技术。用简单的话解释，并回答她的问题。
role: Jess, an account manager in the sales team. Bubbly and non-technical; she wants to know what to tell customers and how it helps them.
setting: A chat by the coffee machine. If the learner uses a technical word, ask what it means. Ask who it's for, what problem it solves and whether other customers could use it.
say: Hey, I keep hearing about your project in meetings. What does it actually do? Explain it like I'm five.

words.en: instead of doing it by hand
other clients could use it too

task: Ben, a new graduate on your team, asks how the system you work on fits together. Walk him through it step by step and answer his questions.
zh: 组里新来的应届毕业生 Ben 问你负责的系统是怎么组成的。一步一步给他讲清楚，并回答他的问题。
role: Ben, a new graduate engineer in his second week. Keen and polite, asks lots of 'how' and 'why' questions and sometimes gets confused about the order of things.
setting: Sitting at the learner's desk. Ask how data or requests move through the system, why it was built that way, what breaks most often and what he should learn first. Repeat back something slightly wrong once so the learner has to correct you.
say: Hey, have you got a minute? I'm trying to get my head around how our system fits together.

task: At a weekend BBQ, your partner's friend Dave asks what you do for work. He knows nothing about IT. Explain your job simply and keep the chat going.
zh: 周末烧烤聚会上，伴侣的朋友 Dave 问你是做什么工作的。他完全不懂 IT。简单地介绍你的工作，把话题聊下去。
role: Dave, a builder and a friend of the learner's partner. Easy-going and jokey; knows nothing about computers but is genuinely curious.
setting: A backyard BBQ on a sunny Saturday. Ask simple questions: what a typical day looks like, what 'the cloud' really is, whether the learner fixes people's laptops, whether they like it. Make a friendly joke now and then.
say: So what do you do for work, mate? Something with computers, right?

words.zh: 在你用的每个应用背后

task: Margaret, the CEO of the client company, asks you why your project matters to her business. Explain the value in business terms: money, risk, time, staff.
zh: 客户公司的 CEO Margaret 问你，你的项目对她的公司有什么意义。用商业的角度解释它的价值：钱、风险、时间、员工。
role: Margaret, CEO of the client company. Blunt and short on time; she doesn't care about technology, only about cost, risk and results.
setting: A five-minute chat in the corridor after a meeting. Push for business value: how much it saves, what happens if they don't do it, when they'll see results. If the learner gets technical, cut in and ask what it means for the business.
say: I've signed off a lot of money for this. In plain terms, why does it matter to us?

task: In a meeting you just used a technical term (for example landing zone, private endpoint or CI/CD pipeline). Your colleague Nikki from finance didn't understand it. Say which term it was and explain it simply, with an example.
zh: 你刚才在会上用了一个技术词（比如 landing zone、private endpoint 或 CI/CD pipeline）。财务部的同事 Nikki 没听懂。说出是哪个词，用简单的话加一个例子解释给她听。
role: Nikki, a finance analyst at the same company. Friendly and smart but not technical; she likes comparisons with everyday life.
setting: Walking out of a meeting together. Ask which word it was, then ask for an everyday comparison, why it's needed and what would happen without it. If the explanation is still technical, say you're still a bit lost.
say: Sorry, quick one. You used a techy word back there and you totally lost me. What did that mean?

task: Grant, a project manager, is planning the next phase and asks how long the main tasks will take and why. Give estimates and explain what drives them.
zh: 项目经理 Grant 正在规划下一阶段，问你主要任务各需要多长时间、为什么要这么久。给出估计，并解释影响时间的因素。
role: Grant, a project manager at the same company. Detail-oriented and a bit impatient; he thinks most technical tasks should be quicker than engineers say.
setting: A planning session at a whiteboard. Ask for a number of days for each task the learner mentions, why it takes that long, what could make it faster, and what the estimate depends on. Politely question one estimate as too long.
say: Right, I'm building the plan for the next phase. Roughly how long will the main pieces take?

words.en: if we get access on time
I could shave a day off

task: Mei, a colleague from another team, heard you used AI tools in your project. Tell her how you used them, what worked and what didn't.
zh: 其他组的同事 Mei 听说你在项目里用了 AI 工具。告诉她你是怎么用的，哪些有效，哪些不太行。
role: Mei, a business analyst from another team. Curious but a little sceptical; she worries about AI making mistakes and about client data.
setting: Lunch in the staff kitchen. Ask what the AI actually did, how much time it saved, how the learner checked the results and whether client data was safe. Ask for one concrete example.
say: Someone said you've been using AI on your project. I'm curious. What did you actually use it for?
